transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I've been having trouble sleeping for about three months now, and it's leaving me exhausted. It started around the time I retired.
How is your sleep trouble affecting you day to day, and do you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
I'm too tired to work on my allotment, and I tend to doze off in the chair in the afternoon. As for allergies, I don't have any known allergies to medicines.
Can you tell me about any medicines you take regularly or have started recently, and also about any past health problems, long-term conditions, operations, or hospital stays you've had?

I take losartan 50 mg once a day for blood pressure, and tamsulosin 400 micrograms at night for an enlarged prostate. I've also been taking over-the-counter diphenhydramine sleeping tablets from the pharmacy most nights for the past three weeks. Those are my only long-term conditions, and I haven't had any operations or hospital stays.
On a scale from 0 to 10, how bad would you say your trouble sleeping is, with 0 being no trouble and 10 being the worst you can imagine?
I'd rate it a 7 out of 10. I only get about four hours of sleep a night.
Can you describe in your own words what your trouble sleeping is like, where you feel it in your body (if anywhere) and whether it moves or spreads, and anything that makes it better or worse?

It's not something I feel in my body—there's no pain or anything like that. I fall asleep fine at about 11 pm, but then I wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning and can't get back to sleep. It tends to be worse after late evenings watching TV, and better on days when I've been for a long walk.
You mentioned feeling exhausted—is there anything else you've noticed along with your sleep trouble?
My mood has been low at times since I retired, though I've not had any thoughts of harming myself. I don't snore loudly, and I've never nodded off while driving.
What worries you most about your trouble sleeping?
Honestly, I just want to be prescribed proper sleeping tablets. The over-the-counter ones aren't really helping.
Are there any other medicines you take, either regularly or now and then, that you haven't mentioned yet?
No, those are the only medicines I take—nothing else regularly or now and then.
Is there anything else you'd like to add?
No, I think that covers it. I'd just really like something to help me sleep properly.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
